title: Final Fantasy VIII's Theme Song Won a Real Music Award in Japan
hook:
In 1999, Faye Wong's Eyes on Me from Final Fantasy VIII sold over 400,000 copies and won Song of the Year at the Japan Gold Disc Awards. Which game song deserves a trophy?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the theme song from Final Fantasy Eight won a real music industry award in Japan? Back in nineteen ninety nine, Square decided to give the game a proper pop ballad with a real singer. Composer Nobuo Uematsu wrote the music, and the singer they landed was Faye Wong. She was a huge Hong Kong pop star, and the face of the film Chungking Express. The song was called Eyes on Me. In the story, a pianist named Julia writes it for a soldier called Laguna, who never comes back. Outside the game, it became a real hit. The single went on sale in Japan that February, and it went on to sell more than four hundred thousand copies on CD. Then it won Song of the Year in the Western music category at the Japan Gold Disc Awards. Not many video game songs, before or since, can say that. Guinness World Records lists Eyes on Me as the biggest selling video game theme song. Not bad for a ballad written to play over a love scene in a role playing game. Plenty of players still get chills the moment that piano intro starts playing. So which Final Fantasy song deserves its own award? Follow for more gaming history.
